messages.author: 613da93894941704
messages.subject: color with a function
parts:
How can i use ggplot2 to color with a function like i can with plot and col=colors, where colors <- ifelse(x >= 0, "green", "red")

Specifically, I want to color negative values of the bar chart red and positive green:

ggplot(melt(df,measure.vars=c("data1", "data2", "data3", "data4")), aes(x=Month,y=value)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") + facet_wrap(~variable, ncol=1, scales = "free_y") + scale_y_continuous(labels=comma)

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: color with a function
parts:
I would do it by creating a new vector of factors in your data frame, something called "Direction", where that column of data is "Negative" if x < 0 and "Positive" otherwise. Then, with `geom_bar` you would use the fill aesthetic to color on "Direction", e.g., geom_bar(aes(fill = Direction)) and then you can manually denote the colors with scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "green").

Best wishes,
Doug

messages.author: 4f04313c0a6b0f2f
messages.subject: Re: color with a function
parts:
I assume you have received a reply to your question. 

I would create a factor variable for condition number (say 0 and 1) to add to the reshaped dataframe 
colours=c("red","green") # set your palette
yourplot (with the fill or color aes = newlycreatedconditionvar) +scale_fill_manual(values=colours)

Please also see Winston's Cookbook site: http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Colors_(ggplot2)/#palettes-manually-defined

messages.author: da357d1a0f57615c
messages.subject: Re: color with a function
parts:
You can use functions in the aes() setting. Vis:

t = data.frame(x=0:10, y=-5:5)
ggplot(data=t, aes(x=x, y=y, colour=sign(y))) + geom_point() + scale_colour_gradient(low="red", high="green")

Malcolm
